report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of graph_delta.py; enumerated claims in docstrings and comments, verified against code in this chunk.
risks: load_mutations | medium | The docstring says it imports the corpus from tools/gate_discrimination.py, but the import uses a custom module name '_gate_discrimination'; the claim that it is the same corpus is uncheckable from this chunk because the source file is not visible. | Check the referenced file to confirm it defines MUTATIONS and is the same corpus.

load_mutations | medium | The function registers the module in sys.modules before exec, but the docstring doesn't mention that; the comment explains it, so no risk, but the registration is a side effect that could be surprising. | Not a claim; noted as observation.

layers | low | The docstring says 'code.refs.leaky' is excluded because it scans raw source, but the exclusion is implemented by not including it in SCORING_LAYERS; the claim that it scans raw source is uncheckable from this chunk. | Check the implementation of 'code.refs.leaky' in the codebase.

handoff.purpose: Introduces the module's motivation, loads the mutation corpus, and defines the delta data structures and AST-based literal extraction helpers.

symbols.name: DELTA_VERSION
symbols.note: Module-level constant set to the string '1'.

symbols.name: load_mutations
symbols.note: Imports the mutation corpus from tools/gate_discrimination.py via importlib, registers the module in sys.modules, and returns tuple(mod.MUTATIONS).

symbols.name: LayerDelta
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with fields layer, added, removed; provides moved property and to_dict.

symbols.name: DeltaResult
symbols.note: Dataclass with mutation_id, defect_class, file, applied, layers, skipped_reason; SCORING_LAYERS class attribute; properties detected and detected_leaky; to_dict method.

symbols.name: _ast_refs
symbols.note: Parses Python source, counts Name and Attribute references per function, returns a set of 'function->name#count' strings.

symbols.note: Parses Python source, counts Constant values per function, returns a dict mapping function name to Counter of repr'd values, clipped to 80 chars.

symbols.name: _module_literals
symbols.note: Parses Python source, counts Constant values in module-level assignments, returns a set of 'repr#count' strings.

symbols.name: _literal_keys
symbols.note: Combines module-level and function-level literal keys into a set.

symbols.name: _structure_by_function
symbols.note: Parses Python source and returns a dict (implementation incomplete in this chunk; only docstring and signature visible).

claims.text: Import the corpus from ``tools/gate_discrimination.py`` rather than copying it. One corpus, one definition — a second copy would drift and then the two measurements would disagree for a bookkeeping reason.
claims.why: The code does import from that path and returns tuple(mod.MUTATIONS), but whether it is the same corpus as used elsewhere cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: Register BEFORE exec: ``@dataclass`` resolves annotations through ``sys.modules[cls.__module__]``, so a module that is not registered yet makes every dataclass in the imported file raise on definition.
claims.why: The code sets _sys.modules[spec.name] = mod before spec.loader.exec_module(mod).

claims.text: What moved in one layer. Counts plus the names, so a finding is inspectable.
claims.why: LayerDelta has added and removed tuples, and moved property returns the sum of their lengths.

claims.text: Layers that may count toward a detection. ``code.refs.leaky`` is deliberately excluded: it scans raw source, so the corpus's own "SEEDED DEFECT" comments move it for every single mutation and a verdict built on it would be a tautology.
claims.why: The exclusion is implemented by not including 'code.refs.leaky' in SCORING_LAYERS, but the claim that it scans raw source cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: Detected means a SCORING layer moved. It does NOT mean the defect was understood — only that the graph is not blind to it.
claims.why: The property returns applied and any(l.moved for l in self.layers if l.layer in self.SCORING_LAYERS).

claims.text: What the measurement would claim if comments counted. Reported so the artefact has a number instead of a footnote.
claims.why: The property returns applied and any(l.moved for l in self.layers), without filtering by SCORING_LAYERS.

claims.text: THE ARTEFACT THIS EXISTS TO REMOVE. The first run of this module reported 10/12 detected, and every single detection contained the tokens ``SEEDED`` and ``DEFECT`` — the marker words the corpus writes into its own replacement comments. ``graph.identifiers`` scans raw source, so comments are tokens, and the measurement was detecting the LABEL rather than the defect. That is the same self-prediction artefact ``eval/ceiling.py`` separates with its clean and leaky arms, and it is why both arms are reported here.
claims.why: The code in this chunk does not reference graph.identifiers or eval/ceiling.py; the claim about the first run's results cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: Comments do not exist in an AST, and docstrings are skipped explicitly, so what remains is names the program actually uses.
claims.why: The code parses with ast.parse, which excludes comments, and explicitly skips the first statement if it is a string constant (docstring).

claims.text: MULTISET, not a set. Set semantics erase the deletion of a call that still occurs elsewhere in the same function -- and "this function now calls _verify_reachable once instead of twice" is exactly the kind of change a seeded defect makes. Counting is independently correct, not a tune to the answer: it was wrong before the result was known.
claims.why: The code uses Counter to count occurrences and then flattens with multiplicity into a set of 'name#count' keys.

claims.text: Constant VALUES per function — the layer that closes the data-only blind spot.
claims.why: The function walks each function body, counts ast.Constant values, and returns a dict keyed by function name.

claims.text: Three of the five mutations the reference layer missed change no name at all: ``FREE_LANES`` gains ``"claude_cli"``; a host constant gains ``localhost``; an argv list loses ``--no-textconv``. A name-based view is structurally blind to every one of them, because the identifiers are identical before and after.
claims.why: The claims about specific mutations and the reference layer's behavior cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: Constants are a multiset per function, like references, so losing one of two identical flags is visible.
claims.why: The function uses Counter to count occurrences, preserving multiplicity.

claims.text: Values are stored as ``repr`` and CLIPPED: this layer must never become a way for a secret in a literal to travel into a report.
claims.why: The code uses repr(sub.value) and clips to MAX_REPR (80) characters, replacing the tail with an ellipsis.

claims.text: Constants at MODULE level too — ``FREE_LANES = (...)`` is a module assignment, so a function-scoped walk would never see it change.
claims.why: The function iterates over tree.body and processes ast.Assign and ast.AnnAssign statements.

claims.text: All constants, function-scoped and module-scoped, as comparable keys.
claims.why: The function combines module-level keys and function-level keys into a set.

claims.text: Statement SHAPE per function — the layer for the control-flow blind spot.
claims.why: The function body is not present in this chunk; only the signature and docstring are visible.

claims.text: The two mutations that neither references nor literals can see change only the shape of the code: one inserts an early ``return``, the other inverts a condition. In both, the identifier multiset and the constant multiset are byte-identical before and after, because nothing is named or valued differently — only the control flow moved.
claims.why: The claims about specific mutations and the behavior of other layers cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: So this layer records node TYPES and their nesting depth, deliberately discarding every name and every value. That makes it orthogonal to the other two by construction rather than by hope: a change that renames a variable
claims.why: The implementation is not present in this chunk; the docstring is cut off before the end of the claim.

observations.what: load_mutations registers the imported module in sys.modules before exec, and removes it on failure.
The docstring for load_mutations does not mention the sys.modules registration, but the comment does; the registration is a side effect that could affect subsequent imports.
The code uses a custom module name '_gate_discrimination' rather than the actual file name 'gate_discrimination'.
The function _literals_by_function clips literal reprs to 80 characters, but the ellipsis character '…' may be multi-byte; the clipping is on character count, not bytes.
The code in _ast_refs and _literals_by_function duplicates the docstring-skipping logic; both use the same pattern.
